text:
IncidentBot: Pager — Sev2: multiple GPU hosts in us-central-1 reporting abrupt reboots and PCIe AER logs. Cluster= inference-prod-3. Alert threshold crossed: >5 host reboots in 10m. Auto-rotate fallback to smaller model enabled.

Ryan: oncall here, ACKing. Starting triage. Which hosts?

Elaine: I see 3 distinct GCE instances hitting kernel oops + AER messages: gpu-host-uc3-11, -14, -21. Reboot loop started ~1883501000.

Josh: pulling console logs from provider now. Suspect noisy neighbor or PCIe fabric. I'll start live capture of dmesg and system journal.

Maria: rolling down traffic to smaller model for affected routes and enabling per-route fallback to v-small. Notifying routing to shift 20% to us-east.

Ryan: good, customers first — Amy, any inbound reports?

Amy: CS: three enterprise customers flagged high latency, one had 504s for ~3m. No data loss. Tickets created: CS-4721, CS-4723, CS-4728. We told them we're investigating and routing around the hosts.

Josh: pasted logs to GCS: https://storage.cloud/reports/1883501234/dmesg.txt (rotating link). Key excerpts below: 

```
[  123.456789] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0000e000
[  123.456792] NVRM: GPU 0000:04:00.0: GPU has ECC errors, single-bit
[  124.001234] nvidia 0000:04:00.0: GPU fault: 0x50f7
[  125.000000] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000008
[  125.000001] kernel: ---[ end trace 8f4a1234abcd5678 ]---
```

Ryan: that kernel oops aligns with the reboot window. Are these the same HW model?

Elaine: all N2-standard + A100s from the same zone. Firmware versions differ slightly across hosts. Host-level ECC counts increased prior to the oops.

Maria: I captured inference runtime logs — KV cache misses spiking then timeouts for model shards. Looks correlated with host reboot time.

Ryan: mitigation plan: 1) cordon/drain affected hosts, 2) spin up replacement nodes in us-east and move traffic, 3) open provider P1 support case and request host diag (MC ticket), 4) collect full nvml and sysfs dumps.

Josh: executing: `kubectl cordon gpu-host-uc3-11 && kubectl drain gpu-host-uc3-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting now.

DeployBot: Automated action: started new node group scale-up (+6 A100 nodes) in us-east-1 to absorb traffic.

Amy: CS update ready to send — want wording: "We're mitigating by routing traffic and provisioning capacity; investigating hardware instability with vendor." Approve?

Elaine: approve. Add note about possible ECC/PCIe issue, no evidence of model corruption.

Ryan: provider ticket opened: GCP case 9876543210. Asking for HW traces and nv-host logs; requested live console session.

Josh: capturing nvml and PCIe config: attached snippet: 

```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF
==============NVSMI LOG==============
Timestamp : Thu Feb 12 10:03:21 2026
GPU 0000:04:00.0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            Single Bit : 24
            Double Bit : 0
```

Ryan: single-bit ECC errors rising to 24 prior to crash. Could be thermal, power, or fabric errors causing memory corruption then oops. Hypotheses: [H1] noisy neighbor causing PCIe bitflips; [H2] driver/firmware regression; [H3] failing DIMM on host (rare); [H4] provider power cycling causing transient errors.

Elaine: ranking H2 and H1 as highest for now. Plan for parallel investigations: provider diag + firmware/driver downgrade test on sacrificial node.

Maria: note — we've got evals running against fallback model to confirm output parity. No degradation observed so far.

Josh: provider returned initial console logs: repeated PCIe AER severity increases followed by a watchdog-triggered reset. Requesting NV firmware revision check.

Ryan: internal checklist: a) customer impact log (Amy), b) node lifecycle details (Josh), c) runtime/client traces (Maria), d) provider ticket details (Josh), e) mitigation timeline (this thread). Keep entries incremental.

Amy: customer comms: sent proactive message to impacted customers; committed to follow-up with RCA within 48h.

Elaine: quick repro on a spare node: forced ECC injection shows similar single-bit increments but no immediate crash. Suggests accumulation + workload pattern triggers kernel vulnerability. Filing bug with driver team: BUG-1207.

Ryan: mark actions in thread: ACTION-1 cordon/drain same-zone hosts (Josh) — DONE. ACTION-2 scale up fallback in other region (DeployBot) — IN PROGRESS. ACTION-3 provider diag (Josh) — OPEN. ACTION-4 driver firmware test on spare (Elaine) — IN PROGRESS. ACTION-5 customer comms (Amy) — DONE.

Maria: adding timeline entries: 
- 1883501000: first AER events on gpu-host-uc3-11
- 1883501055: kernel oops, node reboot
- 1883501103: additional hosts start showing ECC increase
- 1883501200: automated fallback enabled for affected routes
- 1883501800: provider ticket opened

Ryan: any immediate risk of data corruption? Maria?

Maria: inference outputs verified for a sample set on fallback. No signs of silent corruption, likely availability impact only.

Josh: provider replied: scheduling host evacuation and deep diag; requested we avoid powering the host to preserve traces. They're provisioning a replacement host.

Elaine: good. For RCA we should capture: nv-host logs, full `dmesg -T`, `lspci -vvv`, kernel version, driver version, and power cycle history from provider. Also gather pod-level timelines from tracing.

Ryan: will compile a timeline doc and assign RCA leads (Elaine infra/drivers, Josh provider liaison, Maria runtime impact). We'll produce a post-incident RCA in 72h.

Amy: closing loop with customers: immediate update sent, we'll follow with full RCA.

Ryan: any other asks?

Josh: please hold on host reboots until provider confirms — they want image consistent for analysis.

Maria: I'll keep rerunning evals on fallback and record perf deltas.

Elaine: adding hypothesis status to thread: H1 noisy neighbor — INVESTIGATING; H2 driver/firmware regression — TESTING; H3 failing DIMM — LOW; H4 provider power — OPEN.

IncidentBot: Incident note: recording actions & participants. Severity remains Sev2. Next update in 15m or on new findings. :rotating_light:

Ryan: thanks team. Keeping this thread as the single source of truth for logs, timeline, and hypotheses. We'll reconvene after provider diag.
